- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in following days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85), model overestimates mean; shift forecast toward lower end of historical range.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.0), model underestimates risk; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility or downward surprise.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price peaks; add 2–5% buffer to forecast if recent sentiment is positive or price is trending up.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after a high, model fails to anticipate; add 1–3% downward correction to forecast if sentiment turns negative or price drops >3% from prior day.
